auth.installation.hero_title: Initialize a fresh Trinacria CMS instance
auth.installation.hero_body: Create the first operator, activate the initial session, and hand control to the admin kernel. This flow is meant for the first boot of a clean installation.
auth.installation.form_summary: Define the first operator account that will own the initial session and unlock the backoffice runtime for the current instance.
auth.installation.highlight.single_windo: The installation endpoint is designed to run once, before the platform starts serving normal operator sessions.
auth.installation.highlight.seed.title: First operator seed
auth.installation.highlight.seed.text: The account created here becomes the first trusted operator of the CMS and unlocks the admin shell.
auth.installation.highlight.handoff.text: After bootstrap, the flow signs in automatically so the backoffice can continue without a second manual step.
auth.installation.highlight.kernel.title: Kernel-driven admin
auth.installation.highlight.kernel.text: Once installed, the backoffice surface is mounted by the admin kernel and follows the same plugin-driven runtime model.
auth.installation.footer: After the first successful bootstrap, this screen is replaced by the normal operator login flow.
auth.installation.info: This action initializes the operator surface for the current CMS instance.
auth.installation.error.already_complete: This CMS instance has already been initialized.
auth.installation.error.server: The server could not complete the installation. Try again in a moment.
auth.installation.error.network: Network error during installation. Check the connection and try again.
auth.installation.error.generic: Unable to complete the installation. Try again.
